description: Structured compliance gap assessment for a slot game product. Used in phase 2 of the advisory engagement (see steering/advisory-engagement.md section 1).
instructions: Score every item as one of: compliant | partial | non-compliant | unverified. Do NOT use a binary pass/fail.
Every non-compliant item MUST record where it would be caught: lab-testing | regulator-review | post-launch-audit | enforcement. This is the information a client needs most when making trade-offs.
Red flag items (see redFlags below) are not ordinary gaps. If any is present, escalate before continuing the assessment.

redFlags.item: Game outcome determined using a non-cryptographic RNG (Math.random, System.Random, FMath::RandRange, rand())
redFlags.notes: Product cannot be certified in any market. Requires core logic rewrite, not documentation.

redFlags.item: Game outcome determined or derivable on the client
redFlags.notes: Product cannot be certified. See steering/platform-systems-compliance.md section 2.

redFlags.item: Production build does not correspond to a valid certification report
redFlags.notes: Running uncertified software in production. In Germany this constitutes illegal gambling.

redFlags.item: Self-excluded or under-age players are able to place bets
redFlags.notes: Licence condition breach. Treat as a P1/P2 incident, see steering/incident-malfunction-handling.md.

items.check: CSPRNG used for all outcome determination
Entropy source and seeding documented and defensible
Spin independence: no state carried between rounds that affects outcome
Scaling and mapping free of modulo bias (rejection sampling used)
Outcome determined server-side and logged before being returned to the client
RNG state modified between games, or a cryptographic RNG is used
Theoretical RTP computed by exhaustive enumeration or closed form, using high-precision arithmetic
Simulation uses the production code path and production config files
Simulated RTP falls within the 95% confidence interval of the theoretical value
Per-prize hit rates reconciled
RTP computed for ALL wager configurations, including the minimum bet
PAR sheet complete (all 15 sections)
In-game RTP disclosure matches the PAR sheet
Probability of winning the maximum prize computed (required for Germany)
Minimum game cycle time satisfied per market (hard floor vs average handled correctly)
Release-and-re-press of the start button enforced; long-press does not start a new cycle
Maximum stake per spin enforced, including age tiering where applicable
Max stake resolvable at runtime where behavioural risk tiering applies (Germany)
Autoplay disabled server-side in markets that prohibit it
Turbo / quick spin / slam stop absent in markets that prohibit it
Jackpot removed AND RTP redistributed for markets that prohibit jackpots (Germany)
Multi-game / split-screen disabled where prohibited
No win celebration where the return is at or below the stake
No near-miss design (Sweden)
Demo mode uses the same outcome distribution as staked play (Sweden)
Deposit / loss / spend limits with correct periods and precedence
Limit-setting default-on with active opt-out (UK RTS 12A/12E)
Limit increase cooling-off and positive confirmation; decrease immediate
National self-exclusion register integrated, fail-closed
Session reminders / reality checks with acknowledgement
Forced break implemented where required (Germany 5-minute wait after acknowledgement)
Net position display in the correct currency
Elapsed time display
All required fields logged, including RNG raw values and intermediate mapping
Logs immutable for the retention period
Retention period meets each target market requirement
Data classified so that mandatory-deletion categories can be deleted (Germany section 6h(5))
Regulator access mechanism in place (e.g. Denmark SAFE / TamperToken)
Clocks synchronised; consistent time base
Submission scope includes RGS, wallet, PAM, jackpot controller and logging subsystem
Stake debit, outcome, payout and log write are atomic
Disconnect recovery: determined outcomes are honoured
Multi-stage feature progress persisted across sessions and instances
Wallet transactions idempotent
Game recall available with required depth and multi-stage detail
Build hash recorded (>=128-bit digest) and bound to the PAR sheet
Runtime integrity verification with fail-stop behaviour
Interface compliance responsibility matrix agreed with the operator, no orphaned checkpoints
Minimum age configurable (18 / 19 / 21) and correct per market
Player age available to the game layer for stake tiering
Identity verification completed before real-money play
Duplicate account detection
Account state machine covers all required states; bet acceptance checks state
Game-layer log fields sufficient to support AML monitoring
Payment constraints implemented (credit funding bans, reverse withdrawal ban)
Data classified with a lawful basis per category
Statutory-obligation processing not based on consent
Deletion mechanism distinguishes retained-by-law from deletable data
DPIA completed for problem-gambling monitoring
Data residency reflected in deployment topology
Cross-border transfer mechanisms in place, including backups and support access
Controller / processor roles match actual processing
Build-to-certification mapping table maintained
Pre-deployment compliance gate exists
Change classification framework in use
Regulatory change tracking process with a defined review cadence
Hotfix path does not bypass the compliance gate
RNG verification report
RTP accuracy evidence
Feature logic description
Paytable verification
Responsible gambling UX design
Error handling specification
Audit log format specification
